detail.title: Mechanisms for Autonomous Problem Formulation and Cognitive Evolution
detail.summary: Autonomous discovery in agents relies on both curiosity for motivation and discrepancy-driven evaluation for validation. Integrating these mechanisms allows agents to adapt their reasoning and learning methods rather than relying on fixed structures. Emerging agentic harnesses such as CVEvolve demonstrate that autonomous discovery can be applied to complex scientific data-processing tasks through multi-round search strategies that incorporate code execution, history management, and holdout testing. Furthermore, the development of an inquiring mindset—traditionally studied in pedagogical contexts—parallels the computational need for iterative, out-of-the-box problem solving in autonomous systems.
